content.summary_of_the_paper: The setting of this paper is the challenging non-exemplar class-incremental learning. The motivation is to use pathway learning to learn relatively independently so as to tackle feature interference problems. Thus this paper proposes a novel self-organizing pathway expansion scheme. Two main technical contributions of this paper: (1) a class-specific pathway organization strategy for incremental learning. (2) a pathway-guided feature update mechanism to guide the optimization of incremental samples. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on four benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
(1) The idea of using pathway learning for non-exemplar CIL is technically sound. The proposed self-organizing pathway expansion scheme could be practically important and useful.
(2) The experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
(3) I think the paper is well organized, clearly motivated, and contributes novelty. 

Weaknesses:
(1) Lack of novelty. Generally speaking, this work is a kind of parameter isolation-based method [1,2,3,4], but introduces the novel pathway learning into incremental learning. Early works need task id to select sub-network for inference and thus can only handle task-incremental learning problems. The problem is that this paper use pathway learning to tackle the feature interference problem, but all previous works seem can also handle this problem. The key is to create task-specific feature space for every phase. On this basis, the success of this paper in extending task-incremental learning to class-incremental learning lies in using three baseline losses [5, 6, 7] (Eq.6 in the paper) to train a unified classifier. I do not completely deny the contributions of this paper, but considering the proposed pathway planner is an additional network to do task identification, the results are not so significant.
(2) The pathway used in this paper is better than the early parameter isolation works in that the sub-network allocation is dynamic. But in recent years, a lot of work[8,9,10] has also allocated sub-networks dynamically for new tasks.  
(3) Lack of clarity. The organization of this paper makes me very confused. I struggle to figure out how and when to train the proposed CPO, PFU, feature extractor, and classifiers. It will be helpful if the paper can provide a complete algorithm and make it clear which parts are trainable in different stages. 
(4) The motivation for using intersection over union (IoU) as a metric to evaluate pathway similarity is vague. Is this a common practice for pathway learning?


[1] Serra, J., Suris, D., Miron, M. and Karatzoglou, A., 2018, July. Overcoming catastrophic forgetting with hard attention to the task. In International Conference on Machine Learning (pp. 4548-4557). PMLR.
[2] Mallya, A. and Lazebnik, S., 2018. Packnet: Adding multiple tasks to a single network by iterative pruning. In Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (pp. 7765-7773).
[3] Fernando, C., Banarse, D., Blundell, C., Zwols, Y., Ha, D., Rusu, A.A., Pritzel, A. and Wierstra, D., 2017. Pathnet: Evolution channels gradient descent in super neural networks. arXiv preprint arXiv:1701.08734.
[4] Aljundi, R., Chakravarty, P. and Tuytelaars, T., 2017. Expert gate: Lifelong learning with a network of experts. In Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (pp. 3366-3375).
[5] Zhu, K., Zhai, W., Cao, Y., Luo, J. and Zha, Z.J., 2022. Self-Sustaining Representation Expansion for Non-Exemplar Class-Incremental Learning. In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (pp. 9296-9305).
[6] Zhu, F., Zhang, X.Y., Wang, C., Yin, F. and Liu, C.L., 2021. Prototype augmentation and self-supervision for incremental learning. In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (pp. 5871-5880).
[7] Zhu, F., Cheng, Z., Zhang, X.Y. and Liu, C.L., 2021. Class-Incremental Learning via Dual Augmentation. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 34, pp.14306-14318.

content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The organization of this paper is somehow confusing. I struggle to figure out how and when to train the proposed CPO, PFU, feature extractor, and classifiers. It will be helpful if the paper can provide a complete algorithm and make it clear which parts are trainable in different stages. 
Nevertheless, I think this paper is reproducible and the idea to introduce pathway learning into incremental learning is novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a pathway-based non-exemplar class-incremental learning method, which includes a class-specific pathway organization strategy and a pathway-guided feature update mechanism. The proposed method considers the pathway information in incremental learning and influences the feature representation optimization. The proposed method has been evaluated on several datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The authors provide the code in the supplemental materials.
2. The proposed method outperforms other methods on several benchmarks.
3. The idea of utilizing pathway information to influence the incrementally learning model is interesting.

Weakness:
The concerns for the proposed method are listed as follows.
1. About the effectiveness of the proposed method on other incremental learning scenarios. There are several incremental learning scenarios (e.g. class/task/domain incremental learning scenarios). Can the proposed pathway-based method be utilized in other incremental learning scenarios?
2. About the motivation of the proposed method. The authors utilize the observations in Figure 1 and propose some new schemes for NECIL. Hence, the experimental results in Figure1 are very important, and “the experiment results are conducted on which dataset and other experiment-based motivation details” should be presented clearly. Can similar observations be obtained on different datasets or different incremental settings?
3. About the effectiveness of the method in real-world non-exemplar CIL scenarios. To my knowledge, the NECIL methods should not store any samples from old classes and then do not need to utilize an extra exemplar memory. But they need extra memory for storing the representative prototypes and still have extra memory costs. As the number of incremental classes increases, the memory cost also increases. The memory cost is often limited in practical NECIL scenarios. Can the authors make a discussion about it?
4. About the experiment setting. The authors mainly conduct experiments in the incremental learning setting where the base phase has several classes. As shown DER(CVPR2021), the base phase may only have 0 classes (e.g. CIFAR100-B0, ImageNet1000-B0). In the B0 class-incremental learning setting, how does the proposed method performs?
5. About the details of the proposed method. As shown in Equation 7, the number of output channels C_{out} of z^j=k_t should be equal to L*Conv_{\theta^{k,l}_t}(z^{k-1}_t). Can the number of groups be equal to the number of output channels? The authors make a discussion about setting the number of divided groups in Figure 3(a) on an experimental scenario. How to set this parameter on different experimental scenarios or for different convolution modules (maybe the first module L=4, the second module L=8)?  
6. About the efficiency of the proposed pathway-based method. The proposed method utilizes extra cost for pathway (e.g. pathway planner). It is interesting to compare the method with other non-pathway-based NECIL methods regarding memory and computing cost.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. Clarity: some details of the proposed method are not clear and the presentation of the paper should be improved. The key idea of this paper is to consider the pathway in NECIL and the related works about the pathway should be introduced in detail. The authors utilize the pathway to enhance the adaptation of the network to new tasks. Some continual learning methods (e.g. [1]-[3]) utilize the adapter module to enhance the adaptation and these related works can be discussed.
[1] Learn to Grow: A Continual Structure Learning Framework for Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting, ICML 2019
[2] Efﬁcient parametrization of multi-domain deep neural networks, CVPR2018
[3] Learning multiple visual domains with residual adapters, NeurIPS2017
2. Quality: the potential of the proposed method is limited in practical non-exemplar incremental learning scenarios. The pathway modules can introduce extra memory or computing cost in NECIL and the pathway-based method can only be employed in class-incremental learning scenarios.
3. Novelty: The idea of utilizing pathway information to influence the incrementally learning model is interesting.
4. Reproducibility: Although code is included in the supplemental material, some key parameter settings (e.g. How to set this parameter on different experimental scenarios or for different convolution modules?) should be described for better implementing the proposed method.
content.summary_of_the_review: My major concerns come from the observations about the motivation, the method details and the experiment setting. The detailed concerns are listed in the weaknesses. If the authors can address my concerns, I will increase my score.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to solve the class-incremental learning task without using old exemplars. The authors propose a self-organizing pathway expansion scheme, which consists of a class-specific pathway organization strategy and a pathway-guided feature optimization mechanism. Experiment results on multiple datasets are provided.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strengths
- Extensive experiment results are provided.
- Detailed ablation results and visualizations are included in this paper.
- I reviewed this paper during NeurIPS. Compared to the NeurIPS version, Section 3.2 is not clear enough. The current version is much better.

### Weaknesses
- In Table 3, the compared exemplar-based CIL methods are too old. Some recent methods (e.g., [DER](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/papers/Yan_DER_Dynamically_Expandable_Representation_for_Class_Incremental_Learning_CVPR_2021_paper.pdf)) are not compared. It gives the audience the impression that NECIL methods perform better than conventional CIL methods. Thus, Table 3 is a little bit misleading. 

- Some figures are still not explained clearly. As I have pointed out in my NeurIPS review comments, Figure 2 contains a lot of components, but most of them are not explained. The figures should be self-contained. However, the current figures are still too complicated without enough explanations. 

- It would be better to merge Table 5 with Table 4. It is good to provide the results on ImageNet-Full. However, there are too many separated tables showing the comparison results with related work. 

- Different tables (3, 4, and 5) contain different baselines. The questions such as “why is PODNet not compared in Table 4?” should be explained. 

- In Section 3.2,  (Hou et al., 2019; Douillard et al., 2020) are not non-exemplar CIL methods. They use exemplars in their original papers. The authors need to cite some NECIL papers in Section 3.2.

### Clarity & Quality: 
Some figures are not clearly explained. The paper is poorly organized and hard to follow.

### Novelty 
This paper contains some novelty techniques. 

### Reproducibility
The authors provide code in the supplementary.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies non-exemplar class-incremental learning (NECIL), where the new and unseen classes will come incrementally and no old data can be retained. The main goal of this task is to avoid catastrophic forgetting of the old classes while the model continues to learn new classes without using exemplars of old classes. The authors propose a novel self-organizing pathway expansion scheme, which consists of a class-specific pathway organization strategy and a pathway-guided feature optimization mechanism to mitigate the update interference between the old and new classes. Experiments are conducted on four datasets and show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by a margin of 1%, 3%, 2%, and 2%, respectively. The paper also provides some experimental results and analyses to demonstrate the effectiveness of each component of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. Existing NECIL works [1,2] mainly focus on enhancing the overall performance by improving the discrimination and generalization of the initial model, which brings a significant improvement in incremental performance. While the authors start from a novel perspective and focus on the impact of incremental samples on the optimization process.

2. The authors proposed a novel self-organizing pathway expansion scheme and pathway-guided feature update mechanism, which utilizes the similarity of pathways to guide the optimization of incremental samples.

Weaknesses:
1. In section 4.5, COMPARISON WITH SOTA, experimental results on the CIFAR100 dataset show that the performance of the proposed method is improved by less than 1% compared with the SOTA method. However, experimental results on the Tiny ImageNet dataset show that the performance of the proposed method is improved by more than 3% compared with the SOTA method. The explanation for this phenomenon in the paper is “Due to the larger size images in these datasets, the pathway independence during the feature optimization is clearer, bringing greater performance improvement.”. However, the paper does not list the image size of the four datasets, or relevant experimental results to illustrate the impact of image size on model performance.

2. In section A.1.1, the paper claims that “random factors have little impact on our scheme”, while comparisons with other methods are lacking.

3. In section 4.1, perhaps the spacing between the captions in Tables 1 and 2 is too small.

[1] Zhu F, Cheng Z, Zhang X Y, et al. Class-Incremental Learning via Dual Augmentation[J]. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 2021, 34: 14306-14318.
[2] Yin H, Molchanov P, Alvarez J M, et al. Dreaming to distill: Data-free knowledge transfer via deepinversion[C]//Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2020: 8715-8724.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is clearly structured and logical, and clearly introduces the task, motivation, methods, and conclusions of this work.

Quality: Experimental results on four datasets show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by a margin of 1%, 3%, 2%, and 2% respectively. The ablation experiment and visualization results in this paper also fully demonstrate the effectiveness of each component of the proposed method.

Novelty: The authors proposed a novel self-organizing pathway expansion scheme in which a progressive decoupling optimization is accomplished by a class-specific pathway organization strategy. And the authors proposed a novel pathway-guided feature update mechanism, which utilizes the similarity of pathways to guide the optimization of incremental samples.

Reproducibility: Although the code for this paper is not open source, the authors provide a lot of specific implementation details and it should not be particularly difficult to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors propose a novel self-organizing pathway expansion scheme, which consists of a class-specific pathway organization strategy and a pathway-guided feature optimization mechanism to mitigate the update interference between the old and new classes. Experiments are conducted on four datasets and show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by a margin of 1%, 3%, 2%, and 2%, respectively. In addition, the experiment of the paper is sufficient. The authors perform a series of ablation experiments and visualization work to illustrate the effectiveness of the various components of the proposed method. Finally, the paper is clearly structured and logical, and clearly introduces the task, motivation, methods, and conclusions of this work.

content.title: Self-Organizing Pathway Expansion for Non-Exemplar Incremental Learning
content.abstract: Non-exemplar class-incremental learning aims to recognize both the old and new classes without access to old class samples. The conflict between old and new class optimization is exacerbated since the shared neural pathways can only be differentiated by the incremental samples. To address this problem, we propose a novel self-organizing pathway expansion scheme. Our scheme consists of a class-specific pathway organization strategy that decouples the optimization pathway of different classes to enhance the independence of the feature representation, and a pathway-guided feature optimization mechanism to mitigate the update interference between the old and new classes. Extensive experiments on four datasets demonstrate superior incremental performance, outperforming the state-of-the-art methods by a margin of 1%, 3%, 2% and 2%, respective.
